title: Stigmasterol glucoside attenuates RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by suppressing MAPK and STAT3 signaling pathways: an integrative pharmacological study.
authors: Jiang, Yiwei; Jin, Zhiyu; Guo, Kui; Wang, Maihuan; Cao, Zhen
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨植物甾醇糖苷抑制破骨细胞分化，核心是MAPK/STAT3信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且方法为网络药理学和分子对接（针对小分子-蛋白），无AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disease characterized by excessive osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Stigmasterol glucoside (SG), a glycosylated phytosterol with enhanced hydrophilicity, has shown potential anti-inflammatory activities, but its role in bone metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of SG on osteoclastogenesis. An integrative pharmacological strategy was employed, combining network pharmacology and molecular docking to predict potential targets. These predictions were validated using primary bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs). Osteoclast differentiation and function were assessed via TRAcP staining, F-actin ring immunofluorescence, and bone resorption pit assays. Molecular mechanisms were elucidated using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and luciferase reporter assays. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified MAPK and STAT3 signaling axes as the core targets of SG, with high binding affinities for MAP2K1, JAK2, and STAT3. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SG dose-dependently inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and bone resorptive activity without cytotoxicity. At the molecular level, SG suppressed the expression and transcriptional activity of the master regulators NFATc1 and c-Fos, leading to the downregulation of essential functional markers. Further mechanistic investigations revealed that these inhibitory effects were driven by the attenuation of early-stage phosphorylation in the MAPK (p38, JNK, and ERK) and STAT3 signaling axes. SG effectively suppresses osteoclastogenesis and resorptive function by simultaneously intercepting the MAPK and STAT3/NFATc1 signaling axes. These findings provide experimental evidence that SG is a promising natural pharmacological candidate for the treatment of osteoporosis and bone loss-related disorders.
abstract_zh: 骨质疏松症是一种代谢性骨病，其特征为破骨细胞介导的骨吸收过度。豆甾醇葡萄糖苷（SG）是一种糖基化植物甾醇，具有增强的亲水性，已显示出潜在的抗炎活性，但其在骨代谢中的作用在很大程度上尚未被探索。本研究旨在探讨SG对破骨细胞生成的影响及其潜在机制。采用整合药理学策略，结合网络药理学和分子对接来预测潜在靶点。这些预测使用原代骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMMs）进行验证。通过TRAcP染色、F-actin环免疫荧光和骨吸收陷窝实验评估破骨细胞分化和功能。使用RT-qPCR、Western blotting和荧光素酶报告基因实验阐明分子机制。网络药理学和分子对接确定MAPK和STAT3信号轴为SG的核心靶点，对MAP2K1、JAK2和STAT3具有高结合亲和力。体外实验表明，SG以剂量依赖性方式抑制RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化和骨吸收活性，且无细胞毒性。在分子水平上，SG抑制主调控因子NFATc1和c-Fos的表达及转录活性，导致关键功能标志物的下调。进一步的机制研究表明，这些抑制作用由MAPK（p38、JNK和ERK）和STAT3信号轴早期阶段磷酸化的减弱所驱动。SG通过同时阻断MAPK和STAT3/NFATc1信号轴，有效抑制破骨细胞生成和吸收功能。这些发现为SG作为治疗骨质疏松症和骨丢失相关疾病的潜在天然药物候选物提供了实验证据。
